data.name: Index_PageDescription
data.value: Learn about the page templates included in the GCFoundation framework. Page templates are pre-built pages that combine GCFoundation and GC Design System components for common presentations. They’re fully responsive for multi-device use. Their page structures support a predictable, recognizable, and accessible user experience.

data.name: Error_Intro
data.value: <gcds-text>The GCFoundation framework provides you with an error page template that can be customized to deliver the message you want to send your users when they hit a road-block.</gcds-text> <gcds-text>The framework also includes two (2) error pages out-of-the-box. Refer to the <gcds-link href="{0}">{1}</gcds-link> section for more information. These packaged error pages can be configured to gracefully handle any unhandled exceptions thrown by your application.</gcds-text>

data.name: Basic_WhenToUse
data.value: For use on ASP.Net GC applications. The basic page template is for non-specialized pages across Canada.ca and is an optional template. It has the starting elements needed for a simple page and those required for most GC pages and applications. You can use it as a canvas to add or combine components from GCFoundation (via TagHelpers) and the GC Design System.

data.name: Basic_HowToImplement
data.value: Getting the basic page template up-and-running is mostly about configuring your application correctly. All you'll need to do is follow the instructions of the GCFoundation Installation page. This will load to the underlying _FoundationLayout shared view. Finally, just ensure that you include the following statement in Views/_ViewStart.cshtml to make the _FoundationLayout the default page template for your application.

data.name: Error_HowToImplement
data.value:
Use this template to build simple, bilingual error pages:
  • Set Layout = "_BilingualErrorTemplate" in your error view.
  • Add a page title and a <gcds-notice type="danger"> component with helpful next steps (feedback and a safe link).
  • Enable it application-wide by wiring error handling per the GCFoundation installation page: UseExceptionHandler("{{your-url}}").

data.name: Error_WhenToUse
data.value: For use on ASP.Net GC applications. The error page template is designed to display a generic message to users when the application throws an error or when the user tries to perform an invalid operation. It is a lightweight version of the basic page template and its sole purpose is to redirect the user to a safe location. It has the basic elements of a GC page as well as a <gcds-notice> component explaining what went wrong, a link for the user to provide feedback as well as a link to redirect the user to a safe location.

data.name: Error_Design_UseBuiltIn_Description
data.value:
Instead of creating your own error pages, you can use GCFoundation's built-in error pages. The following sample pages are available to use:
  • Global error
  • Page not found error
Enable it application-wide by wiring error handling by using the app.UseExceptionHandler("{0}") and app.UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("{1}") statements in your application's Program.cs.
